newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales grow 3.7 percent in March - BRC.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales grow 3.7 percent in March - BRC.

text.p: The value of British retail sales grew 3.7 percent in the year to March on a like-for-like basis, down from 4.3 percent in February and 4.9 percent in January, the British Retail Consortium said.
Its retail sales monitor showed an average rate of increase in the three months to March of 4.3 percent, down on the 4.6 percent recorded in the three months to February.
"As in recent months, non-food retailers continue to report stronger growth in sales value than in food retailing, where the downward pressure on prices is particularly noticeable," the BRC said.

Warm, sunny weather over the Easter holidays encouraged sales of outdoor products such as do-it-yourself goods and sun creams. But consumers remained cautious about buying big-ticket items such as audio equipment and furniture, the BRC said.
Andrew Higginson, chairman of the BRC economic affairs committee, said the most striking thing about March was low inflation in the sector.
"Our customers are getting value for money from the combined effect of tough competition and a strong pound," he said.
Retail prices data for the period are due on Thursday and are forecast to show a 0.4 percent rise in the month of March for a year-on-year increase of 2.7 percent.
But Higginson said some retail sectors may have been affected by the May 1 election.
"Whilst sales in general have held up reasonably well, some sectors may have been adversely affected by uncertainty associated with the election."
The March survey covered five weeks from March 2 to April 5.
(SEE ALSO SEPERATE ITEM HEADLINED "UK BRC March retail sales survey - table")
